title: Fixing a free variable lowers the free count
statement: Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, and let $v$ be a free variable of $\rho$. For any Boolean value $b$, let $\rho'$ be the restriction that agrees with $\rho$ everywhere except at $v$, where it assigns the fixed value $b$. Then the number of free variables of $\rho'$ is strictly less than the number of free variables of $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: ρ is a restriction on n variables
v is a free variable of ρ
ρ' updates ρ at v to the fixed value b
replaced:
If $v$ is a free variable of a restriction $\rho$, then fixing $v$ to a value $b$
strictly decreases the number of free variables: $\mathrm{numFree}(\rho[v \mapsto b]) < \mathrm{numFree}(\rho)$.
